newsitem.title: USA: Florida home sales rise 4 percent in June.
newsitem.headline: Florida home sales rise 4 percent in June.

text.p: Florida sales of existing single-family homes rose 4 percent in June, compared to June of last year, the Florida Association of Realtors said Friday.
The median resale price rose 3 percent over June 1996 to $97,000.

The association said 12,554 homes changed hands in June. Florida resales have risen each month in 1997, but June marks the first time in three months that resales have surpassed the prior-year level, the association said.

Sales surged last spring as buyers took advantage of newly lower interest rates. Sales tapered off in June 1996 as the average rate for a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage rose to 8.32 percent. The average rate for a similar mortgage in June 1997 was 7.69 percent.
Increases were most dramatic in the Sarasota-Bradenton area, which saw a 45 percent gain, and Gainesville, which posted a 38 percent boost.

Realtors attributed Sarasota's increase to corporate relocations and a short supply of rental property. Gainesville, home to the University of Florida, is still benefitting from its designation two years ago as Money magazine's "best place to live" in the United States, the association said.

June home resales rose by 24 percent in Naples and Ocala, 21 percent in Fort Myers-Cape Coral, 16 percent in Punta Gorda, 13 percent in Fort Pierce, 9 percent in Jacksonville and Melbourne-Titusville, 7 percent in West Palm Beach and Lakeland-Winter Haven, and 4 percent in Orlando and Tampa-St. Petersburg.
June resales decreased by 33 percent in Panama City, 27 percent in Fort Walton Beach, 13 percent in Miami, 8 percent in Fort Lauderdale, 6 percent in Tallahassee, and 2 percent in Pensacola.
Sales rates were unchanged in Daytona Beach.
